title: Choose the visual world for akshaisrin.live
question: The roll assigned Teach Pendant. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Teach Pendant
options.lineage: industrial robot teach pendants (KUKA smartPAD, Fanuc iPendant, UR Polyscope)
options.thesis: The portfolio is the handheld you use to move a real robot: a safety-yellow, graphite-railed HMI whose program is Akshai, with sim-to-real as the literal interface.
options.viewport: A full pendant face. Top status strip: name, city, build date, a green READY lamp. Main LCD: AKSHAI SRINIVASAN in condensed industrial caps as the loaded program, CE + AMATH @ UW beneath, then a three-row program tree: GM Cruise MLE Intern, UW WEIRD Lab RL research, DubHacks Director of Technology, each with a RUNNING lamp. Right rail: six jog keys A1-A6 that are the section nav (About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Resume, Contact). Bottom key row: two large yellow physical keys, RESUME.PDF and EMAIL, plus GitHub and LinkedIn as smaller keys. The E-stop mushroom is real: it halts all page motion (prefers-reduced-motion toggle). On phones the pendant is held portrait; the jog rail becomes the bottom key row.
options.risk: Reads as a costume if the hardware is drawn as decoration around an ordinary page; the chrome must carry navigation, state, and actions or it is noise. Dense HMI grammar can crush mobile. Yellow-black reads construction site if it leaks off the bumper zones onto content.

raised.raise: Hard-edged screens with real gaps: each section is one full pendant screen, never a soft continuous fade.
Proof on the face: every experience and project shows its stack and one outcome metric without opening a modal.
Genre aisles: projects shelved in three named lanes (Robotics & RL, Systems & Infra, Games & Play) with a one-line shelf-talker each.
Fixed-cell numerals: every readout ticks in place without reflow; one condensed face across the whole board.
One clock: every state change on the page runs on a single mechanical tick, no easing float, no glow.

options.label: Training Run
options.thesis: A career plotted as a training run: reward climbing, honestly not yet converged.
options.viewport: Name as the run name. One large reward-vs-steps curve fills the viewport, each experience an annotated step (Neptune, WEIRD Lab, GM Cruise), the line still rising at the right edge. Beside it the run config table: major = CE + AMATH, institution = UW, roles = GM Cruise / WEIRD Lab / DubHacks. Resume and email as the panel's action buttons.
options.risk: Familiar: dashboards are where many ML portfolios land, and plotting your own life can read as self-congratulation unless the not-converged honesty is visible in the chart itself.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: The resume as a departures board: rows ranked by time, roles as destinations, Present as BOARDING.
options.viewport: A board: YEAR / ROLE / ORG / STATUS columns, name in the header cell, the three current roles flapping into BOARDING, past roles ARRIVED.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and everyone reads a departures board; it says trajectory, but nothing about robots, so positioning is lost.
options.risk: Near-black with one amber accent is the calibration the category already ships; flip counters are a known web trope.

options.label: Noir One-Sheet
options.lineage: postwar crime film posters, two-ink duotone
options.thesis: The figure is small and the shadow is four times his size: the shadow is the trajectory, the billing block is the resume.
options.viewport: Name in condensed caps like a charge read out, a small figure throwing a long shadow toward robotics, the three roles ruled tight in a billing block at the foot.
options.case: A one-sheet is a name card by definition, so clarity holds; the audience does not identify with noir, and cream plus condensed is where editorial portfolios already live.
options.risk: Reads as a designer's portfolio, not an engineer's; the shadow metaphor has to be drawn well or it is a gimmick.

options.label: VHS Rental Wall
options.thesis: Projects as clamshells shelved by genre with handwritten shelf talkers.
options.viewport: Aisles of spines read sideways; pull a box to see the project.
options.case: Speaks to the playful streak but not to recruiters or PIs; sideways spines hide project names and rented-out has no meaning here.
options.kept: Genre aisles with a one-line shelf talker per project.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: The portfolio as a live code buffer edited on stage.
options.viewport: A monospaced buffer at stage scale, the cursor line the current role.
options.case: Hackers identify, recruiters do not; phosphor on black is the dark-neon rut the redesign exists to leave.
options.kept: One shared clock for every state change on the page.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the hacker-terminal portfolio template.

options.label: Glaze River Shelf
options.thesis: Experiences as fired samples, glaze runs frozen mid-flow.
options.viewport: A shelf row of cups, recipe cards beside each.
options.case: No audience identification and no product reading; the flow metaphor has nothing to say about an engineer.
options.kept: Recipe and risk visible beside every sample: stack and outcome on the card face.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Sections as cut blocks of weather stacked with blue voids between.
options.viewport: Stacked cloud blocks, each a section, deep blue gaps between.
options.case: Beautiful and meaningless here: neither audience identifies and it says nothing about the work.
options.kept: Hard-edged sectional blocks with real gaps between screens.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio this category ships, executed impeccably: name, typed roles, social icons, card grid.
canonCard.viewport: Centered name and one-line identity, social row, sections stacked below with a card grid of projects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other CS student portfolio by design.
